facts.text: Silver Beach sits on a bluff along the southern shore of Throggs Neck, looking out across the water toward the Throgs Neck Bridge.
The neighborhood is named for its beach, which takes on a silvery color at low tide.
During the American Revolution, the bluff here was used as a lookout point.
In 1795, Abijah Hammond bought a farm here from the Stephenson family and built a large mansion, which later became the offices of the Silver Beach Garden Corporation.
In the 1920s, the Peters and Sorgenfrel families created Silver Beach Garden, a summer colony of bungalows that residents later converted into year-round homes.
Many of Silver Beach's narrow lanes are named after the flowers and trees that grew on the old Hammond estate.
Silver Beach has an unusual history of ownership: residents owned their houses but rented the land beneath them, until they joined together to buy it.
By the mid-1990s, about 350 small houses lined the neighborhood's narrow lanes.
